recommendation:
Step-by-step plan. Each outward step needs its own approval (G22).

0) Branches. Run `git checkout -b v2` and change `next` to `v2` in ci.yml:5-8. Keep `main` on v1, with package.json frozen at the last v1 version. Then v1 `/ctx-upgrade`, which clones main and compares versions (cli.ts:1308-1321), reports 'Already on latest' and never builds v2 source.

1) CI release job (on the v2 branch, on a tag or workflow_dispatch). Build, then run `git fetch origin release || git switch --orphan release`. Copy only the bundles and manifests (no package.json, because Pi runs npm when one exists). Run `git commit -m "release vX"` and `git push origin release`. Each release must be a new commit, and the version in plugin.json and .codex-plugin/plugin.json must go up. Tags alone do nothing for Codex or Pi, and a moving ref with no version change leaves Claude Code users on the cached copy (host.md:248). Move bundle.yml off main.

a) Version bump. On `release`, set `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` and `.codex-plugin/plugin.json` to `"version": "2.0.0"`. Do not set a version in the marketplace entry (v1 sets it in both places today).

b) Marketplace ref. On main, edit only `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` plugins[0]: `"source": {"source":"github","repo":"mksglu/context-mode","ref":"release"}`, and remove its `version`. Run `claude plugin validate .`. Test in a clean HOME with `claude plugin marketplace add mksglu/context-mode` and then `claude plugin install context-mode@context-mode`. Check that the cache dir shows 2.0.0.

c) Docs + release note. Give the exact update commands.
- Claude Code: `claude plugin marketplace update context-mode && claude plugin update context-mode@context-mode` (auto-update is off by default).
- Codex: `codex plugin marketplace upgrade`.
- Gemini/Qwen: remove the v1 MCP entry, then run `gemini extensions install https://github.com/mksglu/context-mode --ref release --auto-update`.
- Pi: `pi install git:github.com/mksglu/context-mode@release` (checked in source only, so test it live first).
- OpenCode 2: `git+https://github.com/mksglu/context-mode.git#release` (the spike marks this DISPUTED, so test released 1.x and 2.x first).
- npm users: `npm uninstall -g context-mode`, remove the v1 hook and MCP entries, then use the agent's git install.
- Copilot CLI, VS Code Copilot, Kiro, ZCode: test these before you document them.

d) Run `npm deprecate context-mode@"<2.0.0" "v1 is frozen. v2 installs from git: https://github.com/mksglu/context-mode#install"` as the owner, with --otp. Global users see this only when they reinstall.

Traffic job (G23). Add a new workflow with cron `0 3 * * 1` (weekly), `permissions: contents: write` and `GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.TRAFFIC_TOKEN }}` (fine-grained PAT, Administration: read). It runs `gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/traffic/clones?per=day"` and `.../traffic/views?per=day`. recommendation:
Give each agent one pure detect function. It returns {file, jsonPath|tomlSection, reason} and never edits files by default. Rules:
- JSON hook arrays (Claude, Gemini, Qwen, VS Code, Kiro): match an inner command when it contains 'context-mode' AND either 'context-mode hook <agent>' or a known v1 script name under hooks/[<agent>/]. Do not reuse the v1 rule that matches the script name alone (Claude hooks.ts:204-214, Qwen :357, Kiro hooks.ts:98). Remove only the inner hook, then drop entries whose hooks[] is empty.
- Whole-file ownership (delete): ~/.copilot/hooks/context-mode.json, <cwd>/.github/hooks/context-mode.json, <claudeDir>/hooks/context-mode-cache-heal.{mjs,sh} (plus its SessionStart entry).
- Codex TOML: remove mcp_servers.context-mode, mcp_servers.context-mode.tools.*, and the hooks.state.* entries that point at removed v1 hooks. Keep [features].hooks.
- OpenCode: remove the 'context-mode' plugin string only if v2 uses a different plugin id.
- Pi: the registration is the 'npm:context-mode' entry in ~/.pi/agent/settings.json packages[], not ~/.pi/extensions. If v2 keeps the npm name, leave it. Otherwise report it.
- Data dirs <agentRoot>/context-mode/ and ~/.context-mode/: delete (no migration). ~/.gemini/context-mode is shared with Antigravity.
- Instruction files: report only, never edit. v1 has no markers, so match only on the whole-file header.
- Entries the user added by hand (mcpServers, statusLine): report with a fix hint. Do not remove them.

recommendation:
The recommendation still holds. One fix: Qwen moves to group (2).

The owner is right: advice alone does not save context (#1003, #1026, #1212). But a hard deny of the TOOL causes dead ends (#230, #794, #1037, #1006, #1269). v2 policy: 'never deny the user's intent, always cap the bytes'.

(1) Primary: rewrite instead of deny. For flood-prone Bash (curl/wget to stdout, build tools, big find/grep/cat, unbounded commands), PreToolUse returns allow + updatedInput, and the command becomes `context-mode run -- <original>`. Pass the original via an env var or base64, not string escaping (see closed PR #926). The wrapper does three things:
- It runs the real command and keeps its exit code.
- It stores the full output in the session DB/FTS.
- It prints a capped head/tail, a docid and a ctx_search hint.

The wrapper does not depend on isMCPReady (#1053, #1055, #347). It works on CC, Codex, Gemini, Qwen (not policy-owned calls), Copilot CLI, VS Code, ZCode, Pi and OpenCode. It does not work on Kiro.

(2) Safety net: cap output after the tool runs. When a built-in tool's output is over a threshold (8-16 KB), index the full output and replace what the model sees with a summary and a docid:
- Real replacement: CC updatedToolOutput (exact tool shape), Copilot CLI modifiedResult, Pi tool_result content, OpenCode execute.after result.
- Replace-as-reason: Codex (continue:false + reason gives non-error text; block gives an error), Gemini (block reason or tailToolCallRequest to a ctx_* tool), Qwen (continue:false + stopReason gives an error).

This step saves context only; the tool has already run (CC hooks.md:2189). It also fixes the WebFetch artifact-URL bugs (#938, #984, #1006).

(3) VS Code, ZCode and Kiro have no output replacement. Use (1) where possible, plus a per-call (not once-per-session) additionalContext. Hard-deny only known flood patterns, with a reason that names a working alternative. Do this only when the ctx_* tools are confirmed available in THIS session or subagent.

(4) Keep real denies only for the user's own permissions.deny policy.

(5) Measure savings only from bytes the replace path really removed (the idea of open PR #952).
